title: PTY socket protocol handler
description:
Create Unix sockets for PTY I/O that bz connects to directly.

## Context
Each PTY gets its own socket at ~/.local/share/bz/chaperones/<name>/<pty_id>.sock. bz connects to these sockets for terminal I/O, bypassing bzd.

## Implementation

### Files to Modify
- `src/chaperone/pty.rs` — Add socket handling to ManagedPty

### Socket Protocol
Reuse existing protocol from `src/protocol.rs`:
- Input { pty_id, data } — keyboard input
- Resize { pty_id, rows, cols } — terminal resize  
- Output { pty_id, data } — PTY output
- History { pty_id, data } — buffered history on connect
- HistoryEnd { pty_id } — end of history marker

### Socket Creation
```rust
impl ManagedPty {
    fn create_socket(&self) -> Result<UnixListener> {
        let socket_path = format!(
            "~/.local/share/bz/chaperones/{}/{}.sock",
            self.chaperone_name, self.id
        );
        // Remove stale socket
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&socket_path);
        UnixListener::bind(&socket_path)
    }
}
```

### Connection Handling
Accept one client at a time (like bzd does). On connect:
1. Send History for replay
2. Send HistoryEnd marker
3. Stream Output messages
4. Handle Input/Resize from client

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] PTY socket created at correct path
- [ ] Client can connect and receive history
- [ ] Live output streams to client
- [ ] Input from client reaches PTY
- [ ] Resize commands work

## Gotchas
- One client at a time per PTY socket
- bz will need socket path from control socket events
close_reason: PTY socket infrastructure in src/chaperone/pty_socket.rs, integrated in control.rs. Sockets created on PTY spawn.

title: bzc: Server-side vt100 parsing for instant reconnect
description:
Move vt100 terminal parsing from bz client to bzc daemon.

## Current Behavior
- bzc buffers raw PTY output bytes (1MB ring buffer)
- On client connect, replays entire history buffer
- Client's vt100 parser processes everything to rebuild screen state
- First visit to a channel takes ~2s (shell startup output replay)
- Subsequent visits instant (minimal new output)

## Proposed Change
- bzc maintains its own vt100 parser per PTY
- On client connect, sends screen snapshot (current visible + scrollback)
- Client receives pre-parsed state, instant display regardless of history size

## Benefits
- Instant reconnect regardless of accumulated output
- Consistent reconnect time (not dependent on shell activity)
- Reduced client-side parsing work

## Trade-offs
- More complexity in bzc (vt100 dependency, state management)
- Protocol changes needed (screen snapshot format)
- Server now owns terminal state (potential consistency concerns)

## Implementation Notes
- vt100 crate already used by bz, can add to bzc
- Need new protocol message type for screen snapshots
- Consider: send diff vs full snapshot on reconnect?

comments.text:
## Slack-style default display

Per user feedback, the picker should show channels in priority order:

1. **Channels with bells** (sorted by count, highest first) - e.g., `#channel (3)`
2. **Channels with activity** (unreads) - e.g., `#channel *`  
3. **Other channels** - hidden by default, appear when typing filter

This matches Slack's Cmd+K behavior where you see important stuff first, then can search for anything else.

Implementation:
- When query is empty, only show channels with bells or activity
- Sort by: bells (desc) → has activity → alphabetical
- When typing, switch to fuzzy match across ALL channels

title: Test with target applications
description:
# Test with target applications

Verify terminal emulation works correctly with all target apps.

## Context

The definition specifies these apps must render correctly:
- Claude Code
- iamb (Matrix client)
- OpenCode  
- vim/neovim
- tmux
- Standard shells (bash, zsh, fish)

This ticket is for systematic testing and fixing any issues.

## Implementation

### Test Matrix

| App | Feature | Expected | Notes |
|-----|---------|----------|-------|
| bash | Basic commands | ✓ | ls, cd, cat |
| bash | Colors | ✓ | ls --color, prompt colors |
| bash | Readline | ✓ | Arrow keys, history, Ctrl+R |
| vim | Startup | ✓ | Opens without errors |
| vim | Editing | ✓ | Insert mode, navigation |
| vim | Colors | ✓ | Syntax highlighting |
| vim | Mouse | ✓ | Click to position cursor |
| vim | Resize | ✓ | Redraws on window resize |
| tmux | Startup | ✓ | Creates session |
| tmux | Splits | ✓ | Panes render correctly |
| tmux | Prefix key | ✓ | Ctrl+B works (via Ctrl+B b) |
| Claude Code | Startup | ✓ | TUI initializes |
| Claude Code | Streaming | ✓ | Output streams smoothly |
| Claude Code | Syntax | ✓ | Code blocks render |
| Claude Code | Bell | ✓ | Notifications detected |
| iamb | Startup | ✓ | TUI initializes |
| iamb | Messages | ✓ | Chat renders correctly |

### Testing Process

1. Launch bz with test config
2. For each app, run through the test cases
3. Document any failures with screenshots/logs
4. Fix issues or create follow-up tickets

### Common Issues to Watch For

- **Cursor positioning** — Apps that use absolute cursor positioning
- **Alternate screen** — Apps that switch to/from alternate buffer
- **Colors** — 256 color and true color support
- **Unicode** — Wide characters, emoji
- **Mouse** — Apps that expect mouse input

### Debugging Tips

```rust
// Add debug logging for escape sequences
env_logger::init();
log::debug\!("PTY output: {:?}", &data[..n.min(100)]);
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All apps in test matrix work or have documented issues
- [ ] Critical apps (vim, tmux, Claude Code) fully functional
- [ ] Any discovered issues have tickets for follow-up

## Gotchas

- Some issues may be in vt100 crate, not our code
- TERM environment variable matters (set to xterm-256color)
- Some apps detect terminal capabilities via terminfo

title: bzc binary skeleton with CLI
description:
Create the bzc (chaperone) binary with CLI argument parsing.

## Context
bzc is the chaperone process — the atomic building block that manages PTYs. It takes a config file path and runs as a long-lived daemon.

## Implementation

### Files to Create
- `src/bin/bzc.rs` — New binary entry point
- `src/chaperone/mod.rs` — Chaperone logic (new module)
- `src/chaperone/config.rs` — Chaperone config parsing

### CLI Pattern
```rust
// src/bin/bzc.rs
use std::path::PathBuf;

fn main() -> Result<()> {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    
    let config_path = args.iter()
        .position(|a| a == "--config")
        .and_then(|i| args.get(i + 1))
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .ok_or_else(|| eyre!("Usage: bzc --config <path>"))?;
    
    let config = ChaperoneConfig::load(&config_path)?;
    // ... start chaperone
}
```

### Config Format
```toml
name = "user"  # or agent name
mode = "pty-only"  # or "matrix" for agents
```

### Cargo.toml Addition
```toml
[[bin]]
name = "bzc"
path = "src/bin/bzc.rs"
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `bzc --config <path>` parses arguments
- [ ] Config TOML loads successfully
- [ ] Missing --config shows usage error
- [ ] Binary builds alongside bz and bzd

## Gotchas

title: Ignore resize in activity detection
description:
# Ignore resize in activity detection

Resize causes screen reflow which triggers false positive activity detection.

## Problem

When terminal is resized, the screen content changes due to reflow. The activity detection sees this as a content change and marks the channel as active, even though nothing actually happened.

## Solution

When resize occurs on a PTY:
1. Update the activity snapshot to the new screen hash
2. Don't treat it as output that could trigger Pending→Active transition
3. Essentially: resize resets the baseline, not invalidates it

## Implementation

In `Pty::resize()`:
- If currently in `Pending` state, update the snapshot to current screen hash
- Don't change the state otherwise

```rust
pub fn resize(&mut self, rows: u16, cols: u16) -> Result<()> {
    // ... existing resize logic ...
    
    // Update activity snapshot if pending (resize isn't real activity)
    if let ActivityState::Pending { snapshot, .. } = &mut self.activity {
        *snapshot = hash_screen(self.parser.screen());
    }
    
    Ok(())
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Resizing window doesn't trigger activity on unfocused channels
- [ ] Real activity after resize still detected correctly

title: bz-pty-driver: REPL-style interface for agent testing
description:
Redesign bz-pty-driver for agent consumption with implicit screen returns and automatic session lifecycle.

## Current Pain Points
- Must write scripts to files and pipe them in
- Timing guesses via explicit `wait` commands
- Can't adapt based on what's seen
- Manual session lifecycle management

## Proposed Interface

```bash
# Start new session, execute commands, return screen
pty -n 24x120 "send hello\n"

# Continue existing session
pty "send \x02t"

# Chain commands, returns final screen state
pty "send exit\n; send echo done\n"

# New session kills any existing one
pty -n 24x80 "spawn"
```

## Key Design Points

1. **Implicit screen return**: Every invocation returns the screen state after commands complete. No explicit `screen` command needed.

2. **Automatic output settling**: Wait for output to stabilize (no new bytes for N ms) before snapshotting. Eliminates timing guesswork.

3. **Session auto-expiry**: `--expire=N` (default 300s). Daemon times out on its own. No "quit" or "done" needed.

4. **`-n WxH` flag**: Starts fresh session at given size, killing any existing session first.

5. **Cursor metadata**: Always include cursor position in output (row, col).

6. **Background daemon**: Session persists between invocations via socket/background process.

## Example Workflow

```bash
pty -n 24x120 ""              # Start bz, see initial screen
pty "send exit\n"             # Exit shell, see respawn
pty "send \x02t"              # Leader+t, see new terminal
pty -n 30x100 ""              # Resize test - new session
# ... walk away, session expires after 5 min
```

title: Content-based activity detection with settling
description:
# Content-based activity detection with settling

Current activity detection marks ANY output as activity, but transient changes (tmux redraw, echo+clear) shouldn't count.

## Problem

- Adding a tmux tab triggers activity in unrelated PTYs
- `echo foo; clear` shows activity even though screen is unchanged
- Makes activity indicators useless due to false positives

## Solution

Change from byte-based to content-based detection with settling:

1. **Snapshot** screen content (hash) when output starts on unfocused PTY
2. **Wait** for settle time (~500ms) 
3. **Compare** - only mark Active if final screen differs from snapshot
4. **Revoke** - if buffer returns to original within window, stay Idle

## Implementation

```rust
pub enum ActivityState {
    Idle,
    Pending { since: Instant, snapshot: u64 },  // waiting to settle
    Active(u32),  // confirmed + bell count
}
```

- In process_output: Idle→Pending on first output, capture screen hash
- In render loop: check Pending, promote to Active if settled AND different
- Bell detection remains immediate (bells are always intentional)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] tmux tab-add doesn't trigger cross-PTY activity
- [ ] `echo foo; clear` doesn't show activity
- [ ] `echo foo` (permanent change) does show activity
- [ ] Bells still show immediately
close_reason: Closed

title: Conduit process spawning
description:
Spawn Conduit as a managed subprocess when bzd starts.

## Context
bzd needs to start Conduit before accepting connections. Conduit runs as a separate process, managed by bzd.

## Implementation

### Files to Modify
- `src/daemon/conduit.rs` — Add spawn logic
- `src/bin/bzd.rs` — Call conduit spawn before main loop

### Spawn Pattern
```rust
use std::process::{Command, Child};

pub struct ConduitProcess {
    child: Child,
    config_path: PathBuf,
}

impl ConduitProcess {
    pub fn spawn(config_path: &Path) -> Result<Self> {
        let child = Command::new("conduit")
            .arg("--config")
            .arg(config_path)
            .spawn()?;
        Ok(Self { child, config_path: config_path.to_owned() })
    }
}
```

### Patterns to Follow
See `src/daemon/pty_manager.rs:ManagedPty::spawn()` for similar process management patterns.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Conduit process starts when bzd starts
- [ ] PID tracked for later management
- [ ] Spawn failure returns clear error

## Gotchas
- Conduit binary must be on PATH or use absolute path
- May need short delay after spawn before Conduit is ready
close_reason: Implemented in src/daemon/conduit.rs and integrated in src/bin/bzd.rs

title: Attach/detach notifications
description:
Send attach/detach events to bzd when PTY state changes.

## Audit Findings (2026-01-20)

**Status: ~70% DONE**

### What's Implemented ✅
1. **Protocol defined** (`src/chaperone/protocol.rs`):
   - `PtyAttached { pty_id, room_id, socket }`
   - `PtyDetached { pty_id, room_id }`

2. **PtyAttached working**:
   - Chaperone sends notification when PTY spawns
   - `user_chaperone.spawn_pty()` waits for it and returns socket path
   - bz uses this to establish connections

### What's Missing ❌
1. **PtyDetached not sent** when PTY exits/is killed
2. **bzd doesn't handle notifications** - no room-to-PTY mapping updates
3. **No cleanup signaling** - bzd can't track stale PTY references

### Remaining Work
- Send `PtyDetached` in chaperone PTY management when PTY exits
- Wire up bzd control socket listener to handle these messages
- Update bzd's room-to-PTY mapping on receipt
- Handle disconnect scenarios gracefully

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Attach notification sent when PTY spawns
- [ ] Detach notification sent when PTY exits
- [x] Notifications include socket path
- [ ] bzd receives and processes notifications
close_reason: Implemented PtyExited on PTY socket (pty_socket.rs) and PtyDetached on control socket (control.rs). Client-side handling already existed. Remaining: UserChaperone listener for control socket notifications (future work).

title: Conduit health check loop
description:
Implement health checking for Conduit process.

## Context
bzd needs to detect if Conduit crashes or becomes unresponsive. Health checks verify both process liveness and API responsiveness.

## Implementation

### Files to Modify
- `src/daemon/conduit.rs` — Add health check logic

### Health Check Pattern
```rust
impl ConduitProcess {
    pub fn is_healthy(&mut self) -> bool {
        // Check process still running
        match self.child.try_wait() {
            Ok(Some(_)) => return false, // Process exited
            Ok(None) => {} // Still running
            Err(_) => return false,
        }
        
        // Check API responding (non-blocking)
        // GET http://localhost:8448/_matrix/client/versions
        true
    }
}
```

### Integration Point
Health check runs in bzd main loop, similar to PTY polling in `src/daemon/mod.rs:run()` (line 142-161).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Detects Conduit process exit
- [ ] Detects unresponsive API (timeout)
- [ ] Logs health check failures
- [ ] Does not block main loop

## Gotchas
- HTTP check needs async/non-blocking — consider reqwest with timeout
- Avoid checking too frequently (every 5-10 seconds is fine)
close_reason: Implemented in src/daemon/conduit.rs and integrated in src/bin/bzd.rs
